To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermal conductance of a support post is about 20% higher than predicted by thermal design calculations.

the measured heat inleak of the magnet support post is in the range 0.2–0.4 W at 80 K and 0.2 W at 4.2 and 1.9 K, and that the heat inleak at 80 K is mainly due to the support post, while that at 4.3 and 1.85 K is due to the support flange.
we can perform heat inleak and heat load measurements with an accuracy of ± 0.1 W at 1.8 and 4.2K and ± 0.2 W at 80K, and that the heat load measurements agree well with design calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermal design, construction and qualification of components for use in the LHC helium cryostats, and the thermal design of the helium cryostats themselves.
precision measurements of heat inleak on cryogenic components, and the development of a thermal qualification method for components for the LHC cryogenic system.

the development of a measurement system for the thermal qualification of components in the LHC project, with particular emphasis on the measurement of the thermal conductivity of materials at cryogenic temperatures and the thermal characterization of components in a cryostat environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermal qualification of the prototype magnet support post was successful.
our experimental measurements are consistent with the design calculations, and that our measurement system is suitable for thermal characterisation of components for the LHC cryogenic system.
the test bench is a reliable and versatile instrument for precision heat in-leak measurements at 4.2 and 1.7 K.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heat inleak is well below the design values and the thermal performance of the components is excellent.
the measurements are in good agreement with thermal design calculations, and the thermal design is adequate.
the measurements show that heatmeters and boil-off methods are in excellent agreement, and that heat loads in the LHC magnet supports are well within specifications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat inleak from a cryogenic system can be measured to within a few percent accuracy.
the design of the thermal insulation of the LHC cryostat is conservative.
thermal design calculations are accurate to within 10%, and can be used to predict the performance of the heat interception system.
